definitions.explanation: Food for soldiers in the field, in historical contexts; by extension, any supply of food needed to keep going. Best known from {兵糧攻|ひょうろうぜ}め, starving out a besieged castle.

examples.japanese: {兵糧|ひょうろう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{尽|つ}きた→尽きる：12365_tsukiru⟧。
⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{兵糧|ひょうろう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{運|はこ}び{込|こ}む→運び込む：30545_hakobikomu⟧。
examples.english: To carry provisions into the castle.

examples.japanese: {秀吉|ひでよし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{兵糧攻|ひょうろうぜ}め⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{落|お}とした→落とす：01246_otosu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われる→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Hideyoshi is said to have taken the castle by starving it out.

notes:
A historical word; a modern army's food is ⟦{食糧|しょくりょう}→食糧：03762_shokuryou⟧. The compound {兵糧攻|ひょうろうぜ}め is the form most learners meet, in history and in period dramas.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {兵糧攻|ひょうろうぜ}め: siege by starvation
- {兵糧|ひょうろう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{尽|つ}きる→尽きる：12365_tsukiru⟧: provisions run out
- {兵糧|ひょうろう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{断|た}つ→断つ：27885_tatsu⟧: to cut off the enemy's supplies
